overview: Meta launches frontier models aiming for personal superintelligence
Microsoft unveils efficient AI chip to reduce GPU dependence
OpenAI’s new FFT research seeks theoretical speed limits

top.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
top.summary: Meta’s Superintelligence Lab released Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, larger frontier models with higher benchmark scores and active‑memory features, priced similarly to top competitors and intended to power its Muse agent.

top.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
top.summary: arXivLabs is a framework that allows collaborators to develop and share new arXiv features directly on our website. Both individuals and organizations that work with arXivLabs have embraced and accepted our values of openness, community, excellence, and user data privacy.

top.title: Muse Wonder Puts Meta Back at the AI Frontier
top.summary: Meta’s Muse Wonder models claim top‑tier performance, surpassing Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 and approaching GPT‑6 Astra, featuring Active Memory and Focus to improve agent reliability.

top.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
top.summary: Meta announced Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, accessible via API and Muse Code, positioning them against leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic while expanding its AI agent ecosystem.

top.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
top.summary: Microsoft introduced the third‑generation Maia 300 AI chip, promising 40% higher token‑per‑megawatt efficiency and up to 7× rack‑scale throughput, aiming for primary inference use by 2027.

top.title: A look at OpenAI’s math that’s claimed computes faster Fourier transforms
top.summary: OpenAI’s math repository presents research on reducing the constant factor in FFT algorithms, exploring theoretical limits to accelerate Fourier transforms beyond the classic 5·n·log n bound.
